messages:
tyler: Heads up — during the staged driver/CUDA push to dedicated pools in ap-northeast1 we’re seeing a slow rise in NCCL timeout warnings and a small number of multi-GPU hangs on h100 nodes. Not widespread yet but trending up over the last 6 deploy batches.

maria: Details? which batches, which image/driver?

tyler: rollout id 2026-03-driver-2.5.1, driver 535.86, cuda 12.2. Logs show repeated: `ncclAllReduce timeout` and `nvcuda: channel stall` on pods pinned to node pools deds-gpu-apn1-b. Mostly 2-4 minute lat spikes then task restarts.

jin: can you paste a tail of the kubelet logs + dmesg snippet from one affected host? quick grep for `NVRM` or `nvcuda` would help.

tyler: pasted below from node gpu-apt-03: 
```
Mar 17 14:22:10 kernel: NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x52:0xffff:0x1)
Mar 17 14:22:11 kernel: nvcuda: GPU X: channel stall, killing workqueue
Mar 17 14:23:12 nccl: NCCL WARN Timeout, retrying
```

lee: That adapter error points at a driver/kernel mismatch path or ABI regression with the kernel we shipped in the image. Which distro/kernel version did these nodes have?

tyler: upstream ubuntu-22.04 image with kernel 5.15.0-88. We did the driver build against 535.86 + CUDA 12.2 as usual. Only difference this rollout included a newer libnvidia-container v1.8.

maria: Ok. Impact looks limited to the new pool (deds-gpu-apn1-b) — other regions/old driver pools no issues. Recommend immediate canary pause + scale down of canary pool to drain new allocations. Suggest also enabling fast-failover to software-quantized model variant for in-flight requests.

tyler: pausing now. ops-bot: action `pause-rollout 2026-03-driver-2.5.1`

ops-bot: rollout 2026-03-driver-2.5.1 paused by tyler at 2026-03-17T14:25:02Z :white_check_mark:

maria: Next steps we should do in parallel: 1) collect full kernel+driver ABI diff; 2) reproduce locally with identical kernel image; 3) spin one canary node with old libnvidia-container + new driver to isolate L1. I can take #3.

jin: I’ll run the repro matrix on gce emu with same kernel and run ncclAllReduce stress for 30m to try to trigger. If we can repro, we can decide rollback vs patch.

lee: If rollback needed we need to coordinate with Dedicated ops for capacity commitments — we have active reserved workloads in APAC during business hours. We should signal a planned rollback window and give customers ~30m notice if SLA-impacting. Also estimate cost of double-running pools if we bring up fallback nodes.

tyler: Agreed. For now I’ll open a short incident and ping Dedicated support to flag possible customer-facing rollback. Keep status updates in this thread.

oncall: Incident INC-2026-032 opened: "Driver rollout paused: NCCL timeouts on ap-northeast1 dedicated nodes". Pager duty pinged.

maria: If rollback chosen: we should prefer a soft rollback that detaches new nodes from routing and lets existing in-flight traffic finish on older gen. Hard rollback only if hangs persist after 2x repro attempts.

jin: repro started on gce-emu-04 — running `./nccl-tests -b 8 -e 1024 -f 2 -g 8` in a loop. Will report within 30m.

tyler: thanks. Also placing a temporary throttle on canary placement: set `max_canary_parallel=1` and `batch_interval=15m` for future pushes until we get root cause.

lee: I’ll draft the customer note if we need rollback; short template: impact, timeline, mitigation, next steps. Share in #customer-success once ready.

maria: FYI cost note — if we need to bring up fallback capacity in another region to honor reserved throughput we should estimate hourly GPU cost + cross-region egress. Tagging finance later if we go >2h.

tyler: update: jin saw a reproduced timeout in ~9m on emu with same kernel + new libnvidia-container. Repro logs match.

maria: ok that tilts toward rollback. Recommend targeted rollback for ap-northeast1 node pool deds-gpu-apn1-b -> revert to driver 535.79 + libnvidia-container v1.7. Lee can coordinate timeline.

lee: scheduling rollback at 14:50 UTC. Plan: cordon node, drain, replace image, run smoke (simple batch inference) for 10m, then re-enable. ETA for window: 20-30m with 15m customer notice prepared.

tyler: ops-bot: action `schedule-rollback 2026-03-driver-2.5.1 ap-northeast1 deds-gpu-apn1-b 2026-03-17T14:50:00Z`

ops-bot: rollback scheduled. Reminder: send customer notice 15m before action.

oncall: Noted. I’ll keep logs and a rollback checklist in the incident doc. Post-mortem owners: jin + tyler.

maria: thanks everyone. After rollback we should add an automated kernel-driver ABI compatibility check to the deployment pipeline and a quick NCCL stress test stage for canaries.

tyler: agreed — follow-up ticket to runtime CI: `infra-2026-587: add kernel-driver ABI diff and nccl-smoke to canary pipeline`. Assigning to jin.

jin: adding now. I’ll also capture exact repro steps in the incident.

lee: I’ll prepare the customer note draft and loop in cs. If rollback goes clean, we can re-run a corrected rollout with a smaller canary and the additional smoke tests in place. :thumbsup:

tyler: closing loop here for now. Will post result once rollback completes. Thanks all.
